name: Infest a vehicle
summary: Usually a small, cheap, fast and fragile attacker (some examples are hero or caster units) reaches an enemy vehicle and attaches to it: it burrows inside, clings on top or welds itself underneath. Once attached it is protected (untargetable in the purest form, or just hard to hit) and keeps working on the host until it is removed or the host dies. The effect can be damage over time, a slow, a blocked ability, a tracking mark, a timed charge or brief control of the host; stealing the vehicle outright is a separate pattern, hijack a vehicle. Removal is narrow, so the latch starts a visible clock that the victim and their team must beat. The trade-off is heavy exposure on the way in for safety once attached.
counterplay: Kill it on the approach: infesters are fragile, so anti-infantry fire and point defence stop them before they connect.
Keep moving and avoid stalls; a pin (stasis beam or EMP) is the infester's setup tool, so dodging the pin is the first defence.
Remove it with repair: a repair station, repair drones, a mobile repair vehicle or an engineer-crewed vehicle pulls the infester out.
Use a self-cleanse on a cooldown, such as an electric discharge, smoke or a hold-to-shake-off input.
Get a teammate to shoot the rider off, or to use an ability that clears the hull.
Teleport or make the host invulnerable, which drops or suspends the infester.
Abandon the host: hold X to bail out and deny the kill (in the RTS originals, owners even destroyed their own infested vehicle to stop a chain jump).
Spread vehicles out so a chain jump or contagion can't spread through a group.

other_examples.game: extra:Command & Conquer: Red Alert 2 / Yuri's Revenge
other_examples.note: The original: leaps inside a vehicle, can't be hit while inside, and pops out to dive the next vehicle if its own damage kills the host. One drone per vehicle; an infested construction vehicle can't deploy. Repair (a service depot, a tech outpost or an IFV carrying an engineer) is the standard way to remove it; edge cases such as the Iron Curtain or a Chrono Miner's teleport also drop it.

sources.title: Terror drone (Red Alert 2), Command & Conquer Wiki

other_examples.note: A flying scout that clings to the outside of a vehicle or aircraft, slows it and can self-destruct a few seconds later to hurt the host and its neighbours. Unlike the terror drone it can be shot off while attached, and repair drones destroy it.

Waits hidden like a mine, welds itself under the first vehicle that drives over it, slows it down and reports what it sees. It does no real damage: a tracker, not a killer. Repair removes it; sensors reveal it and EMP destroys it.

other_examples.unit: Hijacker and hero sniper crew kill (GLA)
other_examples.note: For contrast (belongs to the planned hijack-vehicle pattern): a GLA infantry unit, unarmed and stealthed while idle, that takes over most enemy vehicles on contact; a related hero shot (Jarmen Kell) kills a vehicle's crew from range and leaves it empty for anyone to claim. The hijacker can't take uncrewed vehicles such as drones, or transports carrying passengers; Kell's shot instead forces the passengers out.

other_examples.game: extra:StarCraft II: Legacy of the Void
other_examples.note: Attaches a parasitic cloud to one enemy aircraft that damages it and every aircraft near it over several seconds, so the victim's best move is to leave its group. Damage values differ between versions.

sources.title: Legacy of the Void beta patch notes, Blizzard

other_examples.note: A tether that takes control of one enemy unit for a short, fixed time; control also ends early if the caster dies or the victim gets too far away. Kill the caster or pull the victim out of range to break it.

For contrast (belongs to the planned hijack-vehicle pattern): spartan heroes take over enemy vehicles; the target is frozen during the takeover, which is cancelled if the Spartan dies. In the sequel an EMP leap pins the target first.

shooter_analogues.note: A pilot climbs onto an enemy Titan and damages it from the back (the sequel turns this into stealing its battery and jumping off). The Titan hears a distinct sound and gets a warning, and can kill the rider with electric smoke or by disembarking and shooting them. A friendly rider blocks enemy rodeos.

sources.title: The Evolution of Rodeo in 'Titanfall' (GDC 2017), GDC Vault

shooter_analogues.note: Holding a button next to a vehicle throws the driver out; on tanks the boarder clings on top and punches through the hatch or drops a grenade in. Keep moving, have the gunner shoot boarders, or blow up your own vehicle to deny it.
A dart stuck to an enemy vehicle lets teammates lock on with launchers and shows the vehicle to the team for a while: the tracker variant in player hands.

Small spider robots leap onto players after a one-second delay, screeching as they leap, then pin the victim in place and deal continuous damage until removed. The victim holds the action key to pull it off or a teammate shoots it off. AI-controlled, but a working model of the victim's side.

player_translation.summary: A cheap, very fast, fragile pouncer whose skill is the approach. Once latched, the player rides the host and makes choices (drill, sabotage, arm a charge, leap off), while the victim always gets a reaction window and an escape.
as_user: You buy a cheap T1 unit with very low health and a short respawn; losing it on the approach is normal, not a disaster.

The skill is the approach: flank, use cover, wait for a stalled or lone vehicle, or have a teammate pin it first. The pounce is a short committed leap toward the cursor that snaps onto any enemy hull it touches.

Once latched, your camera follows the host and you still have decisions: hold to drill if your variant does damage (it ramps up), with the anchor variant pick your sabotage on a multi-seat host by where you land (on the turret to jam it, on the rear to cut the engine, on the front to block deploying), and choose when to leap off.

If your own damage finishes the host, you pop out with a short grace period. If anything else destroys it, you are thrown clear at low health and briefly stunned, so your team can finish a host you are riding without killing you.
Against infantry, a pounce should not kill outright as in the RTS; at most it finishes weakened soldiers.
as_target: You know at once: a metallic clang, the hull shakes, a large 'infested' marker on your vehicle and a timer ring showing how long until it is critical.
You always have an answer within a few seconds: hold F to shake it off, drive onto a repair pad, call an engineer, or hold X to bail out and deny the kill.
Your own main gun can't hit your hull, but other seats can help, for example with a close-defence zap from the commander seat.
On a multi-seat vehicle every crew member sees which seat is affected ('turret jammed', 'engine damaged') and can coordinate.
teammates: Engineers and repair classes get a clear job: a repair beam on an infested hull pulls the infester out faster than it repairs.
Escort infantry with anti-small-target weapons screen vehicles; spacing vehicles out becomes a team skill.
On the attacking side a pinner (stasis beam or EMP) sets up the pounce, and a transport can drop several infesters at once.
Friendly infantry in a vehicle's firing seat can shoot an infester off the hull, which gives infantry a reason to ride with tanks.
controls: Move with WASD and aim with the mouse.
Left mouse: pounce toward the cursor, snapping to the nearest enemy hull in a small cone.
Right mouse (optional per variant): a pin beam held on an enemy vehicle. Its range is capped so the pinner always stays on the victim's screen, and the cap is drawn as a ring around the pinner.

While latched: hold left mouse to drill (variants that do damage, such as gnaw). With the anchor variant, where you land on a multi-seat host picks the sabotage (turret: gun jammed, rear: engine cut, front: deploying blocked), shown as an icon at that spot. Space leaps off; with the ticking-charge variant, leaping off arms the charge. With the pin that is two counted keys (right mouse and Space), within the T1 budget, as long as the pounce is the unit's primary weapon; an infester with a gun on left mouse needs Q for the pounce, so it can take the pin only from T2.

Victim, with the universal keys: hold F for a moment to shake it off; it works from every seat and while pinned, and you can drive but not fire while shaking. Hold X to bail out. Teammates: the repair tool's main fire removes the infester.
feedback: Before the latch: a high-pitched skitter and a visible lunge arc, so alert victims can react.
On the latch: a clang, sparks at the attach point, the hull rocking, and an icon on the host that everyone can see from above.
Victim HUD: an 'infested' banner, a direction marker, a timer ring and per-seat status icons, plus an announcer line.
A minimap marker on the infested vehicle for the host's team; the infester's team sees it only with the tracker variant.
A clear sound for a successful removal, and a pop when the infester is thrown out or dies; a radius ring on the ground for charge or contagion variants.
changes_from_rts: In the RTS the infester is untargetable and repair is the main way to remove it. Here the victim also needs a shake-off of their own and teammates a mobile removal tool, because a drive back to base feels like a death sentence.
RTS players mass many drones; here one player is one drone, so a single infester must matter on its own while its damage still leaves a readable reaction window.
The RTS drone is passive once inside; a player needs decisions while latched, or it is dull.
Instant infantry kills are fine against computer-controlled squads but frustrating against people; soften or remove them.
Chain jumps must be capped and stacking blocked (one infester per host), so a cheap T1 can't wipe a T3 convoy.
The approach and the attached state must be readable from above: tells, sounds and icons, since the camera can't show the inside of a vehicle.
In a browser game, snapping onto a fast vehicle must be decided by the server with lag compensation, or pounces will feel random.

Add a re-latch rule, since a shaken-off infester can try again: after leaving a host for any reason it is locked out of latching onto that same host for a short time, and the victim's shake-off always recharges faster than that lockout.

team_play.notes: Both teams get jobs: attackers combine a pinner, a carrier and the infester, and a tracker infester spots the host for its team; defenders need escorts, a repair class, crews that coordinate and riders in firing seats who shoot infesters off.

notes: Attaching is simple in a top-down game: follow the host's position and show an icon instead of climbing animations.
The state machine has many edge cases: approach, pounce, attached, thrown clear when the host dies, removed, shaken off, teleported, re-latch lockout, host changes seat or bails out.
Networking a pounce onto a moving vehicle in a browser game needs server authority and lag compensation.
Many systems must respect the latch: repair tools, EMP and freeze effects, deploy and transform locks, teleports, invulnerability.
UI on both sides: the attacker's latched HUD, the victim's banner and seat icons, team markers and the minimap.
An untargetable infester with guaranteed damage and no self-counter leaves the victim no agency; inside versus targetable is the main tuning lever (RA3 changed it between patches).
A cheap T1 that kills T3 vehicles, especially with chain jumps through packed groups.
Stacking several infesters on one host, or a pin-plus-latch loop that locks a vehicle down completely.
Control variants hand a cheap unit an expensive vehicle's gun, so tethered control stays short and weapon-only; stealing the whole vehicle belongs to a separate pattern, hijack a vehicle.
If only one class can remove infesters, teams without it have no answer; always pair it with a self-cleanse.
A tiny infester on a large vehicle is easy to lose from above, and an inside attachment is invisible without an icon.
Players must be able to tell an infested friendly vehicle from a hijacked one.
Each crew member needs to see which seat is affected, not just falling health.
Whether shooting the infester also hurts the host must be obvious.

variants.name: Gnaw from inside
variants.summary: Steady damage from inside until the host dies or the infester is removed; can't be shot while inside.

variants.name: Anchor
variants.summary: Little or no damage; it slows the host, blocks its deploying or transforming, or jams its gun, and on a multi-seat host where it lands picks which, so teammates can catch it.
variants.seen_in: RA3 burst drone, Firestorm limpet drone

variants.name: Parasite tracker
variants.summary: Shows the host to the infester's team or enables lock-on; lasts long or until cleansed.
variants.seen_in: Firestorm limpet drone, Battlefield tracer dart

variants.name: Chain jump
variants.summary: If its own damage kills the host it pops out unharmed and can dive the next vehicle (two jumps at most); if anything else kills the host it is thrown clear at low health instead of dying with it.

variants.name: Ticking charge
variants.summary: Latches, then arms a charge as it leaps off; the charge detonates after a short fuse, hurting the host and nearby vehicles, and the victim gets a window to shake it off or spread out.
variants.seen_in: RA3 burst drone (Halo's grenade dropped into a tank's hatch is a looser, player-planted version)

variants.name: Pin then pounce
variants.summary: A ranged pin holds the vehicle first so the latch lands safely; can be split between two teammates. The pin never blocks the victim's shake-off.
variants.seen_in: RA3 terror drone stasis ray, Halo plasma-pistol EMP before boarding

variants.name: Grab and run
variants.summary: A brief latch that rips a resource out of the host (a battery, a shield) after a short, visible pull that a quick shake-off stops; the thief then leaps off, the host can chase it, and the stolen resource can power up a friendly vehicle.

variants.name: Mine latch
variants.summary: You plant up to two hidden latch-mines; the first enemy vehicle to drive over one is tagged (tracker) or slowed (anchor), never gnawed, and you get a ping. You never wait inside the mine yourself.

adds_strengths.why: Works while you are elsewhere: the first vehicle over a hidden mine is tagged or slowed, and you get a ping.

adds_weaknesses.why: A mine sits still and does nothing until a vehicle drives over it; a driver who spots it goes around it or shoots it.

variants.name: Contagion
variants.summary: The latched effect also hurts the host's allies nearby, so the victim's best move is to leave its group.

variants.name: Tethered control
variants.summary: Latches on and takes over only the host's weapon, never its movement, for a few seconds at most; it ends at once if the infester is shaken off, repaired off or killed, and the victim can drive the whole time.

adds_strengths.why: While latched it is hard to hit and keeps working until the host shakes it off, gets repaired or a teammate removes it.

adds_weaknesses.why: It has to reach touching distance, so it is exposed on the way in.

counters.why: Lone or slow vehicles without an escort or a cleanse are its prey.

countered_by.why: Sustained anti-infantry fire stops a fragile infester before it connects.
Repair tools pull the infester out of the host.
Out of its reach: it can't latch onto or hit aircraft in flight, and they can shoot it freely.

open_questions: Should the infester sit inside the vehicle (untargetable, needs a cleanse or repair) or on top (teammates can shoot it off)?
Should a cheap infester be able to kill a T3 vehicle at all, or only sabotage and mark it?
How long should the victim's reaction window be? This needs playtesting.

shooter_fit.reason: A direct player-versus-player duel with a clear tell, a reaction window and a team rescue; Titanfall's rodeo shows it already works in a shooter.
